## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
This bug was introduced in #37191. The problem is that the `get_capabilities` function uses discovery protocol, which does not always work when the yeelight devices and the HA are in different subnets. Therefore, `get_capabilities` is now optional. `get_capabilities` provides some useful information, like the model and the unique ID of a device. Now when `get_capabilities` failed, we'll fall back to use properties to guess the model of the device, which is the same behavior as the code before #37191. Also, since we are not always able to get yeelight unique IDs, config entry IDs are now used as a fallback for entity and device unique IDs.

Another change is that since getting unique IDs and models are not always possible, we cannot always generate a unique default name for each device. Therefore, `name` is moved from options flow to the main flow. This will be migrated automatically so current users don't need to do anything.

Hey there @rytilahti, @zewelor, mind taking a look at this pull request as its been labeled with an integration (`yeelight`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L500) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>
Did this use direct non multicast ssdp before? That should work over multiple subnets.

@elupus Yes the `get_capabilities` sends ssdp discovery packet directly to the device, so it works in my multi subnet environment. But it can be affected by, for example, firewall settings. So in some environment it does not work while the direct TCP connection works. Therefore, we cannot rely on that.

Well you always need to open ports in any multi subnet situation. If it works by direct ssdp. I would consider those ports a requirement of the device.

Multicast is different though since it can't be targeted plus it's very hard to route. Especially since ssdp often set ttl=1 meaning don't route.

@elupus Yes I agree with you. But since the integration before the config flow PR (#37191) does not rely on `get_capabilities`. So the config flow PR actually breaks the integration for some users. Since we can still make it work without the dependent on `get_capabilities`, I don't think we should ask the users to do the networking configuration.

This is preventing people from using yeelight. Could we get this as bugfix?

EDIT: For people looking for a quick workaround: I ended up checking out this PR, and copying the entire yeelight folder to the custom_components dir of my HA config. Don't forget to delete that after this is released.

@abmantis I manually replaced the Yeelight component because I can't let my family sit in the dark and also didn't want to downgrade Hass. The fix worked for me.
https://github.com/shenxn/home-assistant-core/tree/yeelight-fix

@lambtho12 To allow the yeelight discovery package, you should open UDP on port 1982. Yeelight uses a protocol very similar to SSDP but techniqually this is not a standard SSDP.

issue_context.title: Yeelight Integration uses SSDP even when adding device by IP
issue_context.body:
<!-- READ THIS FIRST:
  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/
  - Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/releases
  - Do not report issues for integrations if you are using custom components or integrations.
  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
In 0.115.0, the Yeelight Integration was updated (see https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/37191) to use SSDP instead of mDNS discovery. This change, however, also introduced a new behavior, in which the capabilities of a configured device are retrieved on startup.

This capability discovery process is also done via SSDP, which means that the integration can no longer be used in setups where SSDP is unavailable, even when specifying the IP Address of the bulb (in my specific case, I have the bulb in another VLAN, which doesn't get Multicast traffic, and I'm not running Home Assistant with Host Networking enabled), resulting in a connection error.

Given this process is used to find the model and ID of the light (which are specified in the `configuration.yml`), it should be optional (as it used to be prior to 0.115.0).

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Configuration -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.115.0, 0.115.1
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): 0.114.4
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): Container (without Host Networking)
- Integration causing this issue: Yeelight
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/yeelight/
- Network setup: Home Assistant running on "core" VLAN and bulb in an isolated IoT-specific VLAN

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```yaml
yeelight:
   devices:
    10.142.50.18:
      name: Office Ceiling
      model: RGBW
```

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

```txt
ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.yeelight.config_flow] Failed to get capabilities from 10.142.50.18: timeout
```

## Additional information

Punching a few holes through the firewall so the Multicast traffic (and corresponding response) can flow through, and enabling Host Networking on the Home Assistant container restore the previous behavior.

review_comments:
Why do we even allow picking devices? It seems to me that we should just show all discovered devices without needing to ask the user to pick. There is no auth necessary. 

For a future PR, we should consider updating this config flow to support:
 - "discovery mode", it will just add all lights it can find
 - manual mode, user has to put in an IP address

Only because you use discovery mode, it doesn't mean you want to add all devices it can find. Consider shared households with shared Wi-Fi connections, like living communities. Picking is still valid, imho.
Picking is indeed valid. And that's why Home Assistant has features to enable and disable entities. We should not replicate that in a config flow.

I don't want to start a principle discussion about it :) Especially not in a pending PR I'm also waiting for, plus not with somebody having "a little" bit more HA experience than me ;)
However, I would be really annoyed if it just adds everything and I need to delete/disable entities after it again. It's just against my inner will to have something added, that I don't actually want and I have to clean up after.

Again: I don't want to block this here and continue the discussion :) Just my two cents on this suggestion!

FWIW, I gave up on the Unifi integration forever because it adds every device on my network (50+), when all I want to monitor is two devices (phones). Maybe deleting entities has gotten easier, but a config flow that results in 95% garbage that needs to be cleaned up afterwards is not a good flow. I think there should be some flexibility here.

For now, though, agree that just adding all discovered lights is better than having all broken lights.

There was some discussion about this in the original PR adding config flow to yeelight (#37191). Finally we decided to give each device a config entry since it is more intuitive and easier to implement (and maintain).
If we have a unique_id available, we should use it and set it, instead of always omitting it.
Now we use `get_properties` instead of `get_capabilities` to test connection, which does not give the unique ID.
I probably miss the context, but, shouldn't you use `get_capabilities` first and fall back to `get_properties`?

If we just want to test whether the IP address is correct, then using only `get_properties` is sufficient. If you think it is better to set unique ids when possible, then yes we can call `get_capabilities` first.
Removing this property seems to be a breaking change since it will cause the unique id to change for this entity. Is that true?
